title: Control Flow & Functions
relevance: Core C mechanics—branching, loops, pass-by-value, and the call stack—underpin almost every SDE interview coding and systems question.

phases.goal: Establish how C branches, loops, and declares callable units of logic.

must_hit.point: An if evaluates an expression and runs its block when the result is non-zero (true); else is the fallback path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate describes if/else as the basic decision primitive driven by a truthy/non-zero condition.

must_hit.point: A while checks before each iteration and may never run; a do-while checks after and always runs at least once.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate contrasts pre-check vs post-check and names a use case for each.

must_hit.point: A for packs initialization, condition, and advancement on one line, suited to counting and array traversal.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate explains the three for-header parts and why that grouping helps iteration.

must_hit.point: A prototype announces name, return type, and parameters; the definition supplies the body; void return means nothing returned and (void) means no parameters.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate separates declaration from definition and correctly explains void vs (void).

probes: Walk through how if/else, while vs do-while, and a for loop each control execution.
What is the difference between a function prototype and a function definition in C?

hints.1: Start with branching, then how loops decide whether to run again.
hints.2: Compare when the condition is tested in while versus do-while, then what a for header consolidates.
hints.3: if runs on non-zero; while may never enter; do-while always enters once; prototype declares, definition implements; void return vs (void) params.

phases.goal: Explain switch dispatch, pass-by-value, and what a stack frame holds across calls.

must_hit.point: switch evaluates an integer expression and jumps to a matching case; dense case labels can become a compiler jump table for O(1) dispatch instead of an O(N) if-chain.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says switch needs integer constants and may compile to a jump-table index rather than sequential tests.

must_hit.point: C is strictly pass-by-value: each parameter is a new local initialized with a copy of the argument; mutating the caller's object requires passing a pointer (address copied by value).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate rejects true pass-by-reference and describes pointer-by-value to reach the caller's data.

must_hit.point: A call allocates a stack frame with parameters, locals, and a return address; returning pops the frame and ends automatic lifetime of those locals.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names those three frame contents and that locals die when the frame is destroyed.

must_hit.point: C switch does not auto-exit a case; omitting break causes fallthrough into the next case.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate warns that without break, execution continues into the following case.

probes: Does C support pass-by-reference? How would you make a callee modify the caller's variable?
What lives in a stack frame, and why must you not return a pointer to a local?

hints.1: Think about what is copied into the callee versus what a pointer lets you reach.
hints.2: Contrast long if-chains with switch jump tables, then list stack-frame fields.
hints.3: No pass-by-reference—only value copies; pointers simulate mutation; frames hold params, locals, return address; no break means fallthrough.

phases.goal: Compare control-flow and function styles the file contrasts for clarity, speed, and safety.

must_hit.point: Long if-chains over many discrete constants are unreadable and O(N); switch with dense cases can use a jump table for O(1) jumps.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate picks switch/jump table for dense integer constants and if-chains when switch cannot apply.

must_hit.point: Recursion can be cleaner for tree-like structure, but each call pushes a frame so deep recursion burns stack; iteration uses less memory; tail-recursion-to-loop is not guaranteed in C.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate weighs elegance vs stack cost and notes C does not promise tail-call optimization.

must_hit.point: goto is discouraged for general logic but is a legitimate C idiom for centralized error cleanup because C has no exceptions; backward/cross jumps risk spaghetti.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate defends goto for unwind/cleanup and rejects it for ad-hoc jumping around.

must_hit.point: inline requests inlining to avoid call overhead with real type-checking; compilers may silently ignore it for large, loop-heavy, or recursive bodies.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate treats inline as a hint, useful for tiny hot functions, not a guarantee.

probes: When would you prefer switch over a long if-else chain, and when does switch fail you?
Recursion versus a loop—what are you trading, and does C guarantee tail-call optimization?

hints.1: Compare dispatch cost and readability first, then stack cost of recursion.
hints.2: Dense integer cases vs strings/floats/ranges; recursive frames vs iterative memory; goto for cleanup only.
hints.3: Jump table O(1) vs if-chain O(N); recursion cleaner but stack-heavy, no guaranteed TCO; goto OK for error unwind; inline is a request.

phases.goal: Apply pass-by-value, recursion/stack tracing, and related APIs to concrete interview scenarios.

must_hit.point: broken_swap only swaps its local copies; a correct swap takes int * parameters, uses *a/*b (and *b = temp), and callers pass &x and &y.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate rewrites swap with pointers and address-of at the call site.

must_hit.point: Tracing factorial(3): frames for 3 then 2 then 1; base returns 1; then 2*1=2 and 3*2=6 as frames pop.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate walks push/pop order and ends with result 6.

must_hit.point: scanf can modify callers' variables because it receives pointers (addresses), not plain values.
Standard main forms are int main(void) or int main(int argc, char **argv); argv[0] is the program name; main should return int as exit status (0 success, non-zero failure), not void.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate states both signatures, argv[0], and int exit status to the OS.

probes: Why does broken_swap fail, and how do you fix it? Trace factorial(3) on the call stack.
How does scanf modify variables you pass, and what are the valid main signatures?

hints.1: Recall that parameters are copies unless you pass addresses.
hints.2: Fix swap with pointers; for factorial, push frames down to the base case then multiply on the way back.
hints.3: swap uses *a/*b and & at call; factorial(3) yields 6 via stacked returns; scanf gets pointers; main returns int, not void.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: For many discrete compile-time integer constants, especially dense labels, switch can compile to a jump table and jump in O(1); a massive if-chain is harder to read and remains O(N). Switch cannot match strings, floats, or dynamic ranges.

Recursion often reads cleaner for tree-like structures but each call pushes a stack frame, so deep recursion risks overflow; loops use less memory. Some compilers may turn tail recursion into a loop, but C does not guarantee that.

tradeoffs.topic: goto for cleanup vs general control flow
tradeoffs.strong_answer: goto is a standard idiom for centralized error cleanup/unwinding in C (no exceptions), but jumping backward or across complex structures quickly becomes spaghetti and should be avoided for ordinary logic.

inline asks the compiler to paste the body at the call site for tiny, hot functions with real type-checking, but for large, loop-heavy, or recursive functions the compiler may ignore it and emit a normal call.

gotchas.correction: Assignment stores 5 in x and the condition is 5 (true), so the block always runs; enable -Wall so compilers warn.

gotchas.trap: Omitting break in a switch case
gotchas.correction: C falls through into the next case; add break (or intentional fallthrough) explicitly.

gotchas.trap: Off-by-one in a for over an array of size 10
gotchas.correction: Use i < 10 (indices 0 through 9); i <= 10 reads out of bounds and is undefined behavior.

gotchas.trap: Assuming break exits all nested loops
gotchas.correction: break only terminates the innermost enclosing loop or switch.

gotchas.trap: Returning a pointer to a local variable
gotchas.correction: The stack frame is destroyed on return, so the pointer dangles; dereferencing is undefined behavior.

gotchas.trap: Believing same-named parameter x is linked to caller x
gotchas.correction: They are separate locals that only share an initial copied value; mutation needs a pointer to the caller's object.

gotchas.trap: Looping on a hardware register without volatile
gotchas.correction: The compiler may optimize the check away and create an infinite loop; mark such registers volatile.

gotchas.trap: Declaring main with a void return type
gotchas.correction: main should return int as the process exit status (0 success, non-zero failure) to the OS.

gotchas.trap: Mismatched count or types in variadic calls
gotchas.correction: Variadic functions are type-unsafe; va_arg reinterprets memory as the requested type, which is undefined behavior if wrong.

gotchas.trap: Assigning a function pointer with a mismatched signature
gotchas.correction: Signature must match exactly; otherwise calling through the pointer is undefined behavior.
